text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

It is understood that in a meeting last week with News Limited executive chairman Ken Cowley and Rupert Murdoch via telephone, Prime Minister John Howard offered to relax foreign investment rules to allow Murdoch to increase his stake in the Seven Network in exchange for his support of Kerry Packer's takeover of the Fairfax newspaper group. Page 1.

Sydney lawyer Sue Gilchrist warned yesterday increasing disputes between advertisers and their agencies over intellectual property rights to promotion work may end up in the courts. The Australian Association of National Advertisers yesterday released gudelines on the issue, reflecting a need for more information. Page 3.

In a joint statement yesterday, pastoral giants Elders Ltd and Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd said the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission had expressed concern about the companies' proposal to save millions of dollars through a wool handling joint venure. The concern from the ACCC is a blow for the proposed Global Wool Ltd. Page 39.

Canadian media group CanWest Global Communications has apparently lodged documents with the Federal Government proposing to sell down from 76 per cent to 57.5 per cent its share of the Ten Group Ltd after the Australian Broadcasting Authority found it illgally controlled the network under foreign investment rules. Page 39.

United States-based Northgate Communications, which has just entered the Australian telecommunications market, may float within 18 months in an attempt to "Australianise" the company. Northgate hopes to position itself alongside Telstra and Optus by investing up to A$500 million over the next few years. Page 40.

Sunday will be the cut off point for Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd to decide if it will go ahead with its A$340 million bid to purchase the 85 per cent stake owned by United States - based Showboat of the Sydney Casino Management Pty Ltd, which runs thecasino, and the 10 per cent stake in Sydney Harbour Casino Holdings Ltd, which owns the casino. Page 42.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Shares in John Fairfax Holdings Ltd hit a three year high last night on the back of speculation Kerry Packer's Publishing & Broadcasting Ltd will takeover the company under a review of Australia's cross media ownership rules. Shares jumped 10 cents to A$3.27 in what was an otherwise weak day on the stockmarket. Page 25.

Australian arm of British conglomerate BTR Plc, BTR Automotive Asia Pacific, has increased one of Australia's biggest ETM (elaborately transformed manufactures) export contracts by finalising a A$490 million deal to supply an unidentified South Korean carmaker with automatic transmissions for five years. Page 25.

Wine maker BRL Hardy Ltd managing director Stephen Millar confirmed yesterday the company believes strong performance and promising forecasts of double-digit growth will allow it to fend off takeover bids from predators including Foster's Brewing Group Ltd. Millar said directors had successfully created shareholder value to protect the company. Page 25.

Singaporean-based Marsford Investments Pte enjoyed a legal victory over investment vehicle Super John Pty Ltd yesterday when it finalised a A$20.3 million takeover of Allied Queensland Coalfields Ltd. Super John had taken Federal Court action against Marford last year seeking to prevent Marsford from compulsorily acquiring 820,000 shares of ACQ. Page 26.

Melbourne junior mining Paget Mining Ltd is in trouble following the discovery of illegal mining and construction of a treatment plant on a rich West African gold property whose ownership is claimed by Paget. Paget has been fighting for over two years fo control of the lease, but it appears rival bidder Eeximcor Afrique, from Senegal, has already started mining without a permit. Page 27.

BHP, Australia's largest ship owner, has given its support for the package of reforms released yesterday on Australia's shipping industry by the Shipping Reform Group. BHP Transport general manager Bruce McGowan said the reforms gave Australia's shippingindustry "every chance to be competitive". Page 27.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Wages growth data released yesterday showed stronger than anticipated average earnings, pushing wage-inflation pressures above the Reserve Bank's comfort zone, and forcing financial markets to rule out a further interest rate cut for 1997. Page 25.

Following speculation of a possible takeover by Kerry Packer, shares in John Fairfax Holdings lifted yesterday, increasing the sharemarket value of the newspaper group to A$2.5 billion yesterday. The 10 cent share increase came a day after Prime MinisterJohn Howard indicated the cross-media ownership rules may be abolished. Page 25.

The Australian Securities Commission will launch an inquiry into the premature closing of Colonial's share listing, after receiving about 40 complaints from small investors. Despite its prospectus and advertising saying the share offer would close today, Colonial closed the offer on Monday. Page 25.

Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd senior executives will meet today to discuss the company's options with its plans to buy out the management contract of Sydney Harbour Casino. It is understood the withdrawal may take place because of Packer's unwillingness to be dragged through a protracted and long public investigation into his business and finances by the Casino Control Authority. Page 25.

Despite a controversial A$200 million in debt finance from the Queensland Government's Port of Brisbane Corporation, the Commonwealth Bank and Dutch Schiphol bidding group has won the rights to purchase the Brisbane Airport for over A$1.3 billion. The deal has been informally approved by the Federal Government. Page 27.

Ampol chief executive Dr Ian Blackburne has renewed calls for the Federal Government to decrease petrol prices through deregulation of the petrol industry. Blackburne said the key to lower petrol prices was to reduce the number of service stations and reove the distortions created by government setting of the wholesale price. Page 27.
THE AGE

In a report by shipping industry leaders, the Federal Government has been called on to end the monopoly of coastal trade by Australian operators and bring in labour reforms to save the shipping industry. Transport Minister John Sharp said the report offeed "the prospect of future growth". Page B1.

Economists warned yesterday the release of data into Australia's wages growth, which indicated an annual rate of 4.6 per cent, could see a rise in official interest rates. The figures come close to the Reserve Bank of Australia's safety band of between 4and 5 per cent, beyond which it believes growth is inflationary. Page B1.

Despite reports that Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd would pull out of its proposed A$342 million bid for the management contract of the Sydney Harbour Casino, finance director Nick Falloon told brokers yesterday senior executives would meet today to further discuss the proposal and make an announcement on the weekend. Page B1.

Following speculation in the media and on the markets about the future of John Fairfax, shares in the newspaper group climbed 10 cents to close at A$3.27, their highest rate since February 1994. The rise follows news the Federal Government may relax medi ownership rules to allow Kerry Packer to buy the company. Page B1.

The new Ford Falcon to be released in late 1998 could be the world's first car to feature all-magnesium seats, that are being designed and made by local suppliers Henderson's and Australian Die Casters. The breakthrough in the lightweight seats is well ahead of any further magnesium parts. Page B1.

Howard Smith managing director Dr Ken Moss yesterday told a Securities Institute of Australia briefing the company was in a position to make an acquisition of up to A$500 million in Australia, which would reduce the changes of a return of funds to shareholders. Page B3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
